reader.requirement: When FUNCTION MAX is alphanumeric (all arguments alphabetic or alphanumeric class, including groups, numeric-edited items, reference-modified and ALL-subscripted operands and ODO groups at their current size), the returned value has the size of the selected argument-1.

reader.notes: MaxString returns the selected string itself, so its length is the selected operand's length at run time, which covers ODO groups and reference modification. The MAX-to-alphanumeric typing is IntrinsicResultType.Resolve via the catalog row's FollowsUniformArguments rule, edition-blind.

refuter.evidence: Aimed at the returned size where it is observable beyond DISPLAY: maxsz-001 J1 MOVE MAX (W-A W-X) TO X(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT gives [  AB ] (size 3 of the selected PIC A(3)), J2 MAX (W-X W-A) gives [AB   ] (size 5); S1 STRING ... DELIMITED BY SIZE gives [AB |]; numeric-edited arguments are class alphanumeric and typed alphanumeric: E1 MAX (NEA PIC 9.9 = '9.0', NEB PIC ZZ9 = '100') returns '9.0' by the character comparison (a numeric comparison would pick 100), L1 LENGTH 03, E2 MAX (NE1 ZZ9 '  5', NE2 Z9.9 ' 5.0') returns ' 5.0', L2 04. maxnest-001 N3 MAX (FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (W-Y X(4)) W-A W-X) gives size 4, L1 04, N4 MAX (W-X FUNCTION REVERSE (W-A)) gives size 5, R1 reference modification (2:2) of the result 'B '. degen-001 G1 MAX (W-A) size 3, G2 ODO ALL of one element size 2. numplace: numeric MAX as an identifier refused at 85 (numplace-001 COBOL0900), accepted at 2023 (numplace-002). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.23.4 RV3 'the size of the returned value is the same as the size of the selected argument-1'; OK §1989:A.2.2 AR3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or a nonnumeric literal must be specified'.
